Wilderness of Kedemoth
WIL-der-nes of ked-eh-MOTH
proper noun
A tract of wilderness east of Jordan, near the town of Kedemoth, from which Moses sent messengers of peace to Sihon king of the Amorites; distinct from the town of Kedemoth itself.

📖 Biblical Definition

The wilderness of Kedemoth was a tract of desert east of Jordan, near the town of Kedemoth, in the days when Israel was drawing near the promised land. From this place Moses sent an embassy of peace to Sihon king of the Amorites: “I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying, Let me pass through thy land” (Deu 2:26). Israel asked only leave to pass by on the highway, offering to buy meat and water and to do no harm. But Sihon would not; “the LORD thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand” (Deu 2:30). Sihon came out to battle, and was utterly destroyed, and his land became the first inheritance of Israel east of Jordan. The wilderness of Kedemoth thus sets before us a solemn mystery: the genuine offer of peace, freely made and wickedly refused, and behind the refusal the sovereign hand of God, who hardened Sihon’s heart in righteous judgment for the fulfilling of His purpose. The offer was sincere; the refusal was Sihon’s own wickedness; and yet God overruled it all, hardening whom He would and delivering the enemy into Israel’s hand. The believer marvels at a sovereignty that leaves the sinner without excuse and yet accomplishes the eternal counsel of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A wilderness east of Jordan whence Moses sent peace to Sihon, who refused; a witness to the offer of peace refused and God’s sovereign hardening. Distinct from the town of Kedemoth.

WILDERNESS OF KEDEMOTH, a desert east of Jordan, near the town of Kedemoth.

Moses sent messengers of peace to Sihon from it (Deu 2:26).

Israel asked only leave to pass through on the highway.

Sihon refused, for the LORD hardened his spirit (Deu 2:30).

Sihon was destroyed, and his land became Israel’s. Distinct from the town of Kedemoth.

📖 Key Scripture

Deu 2:26 — "And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,"

Deu 2:27 — "Let me pass through thy land: I will go along by the high way , I will neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left."

Deu 2:30 — "But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the LORD thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day."

Rom 9:18 — "Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A wilderness of Scripture; it recovers the mystery of the sincere offer of peace refused, and the sovereign hardening of God who leaves the sinner without excuse.

expand to see more

The wilderness of Kedemoth faces no postmodern redefinition, though it must be distinguished from the town of Kedemoth. The truth its embassy carries answers both the notion that God’s offers are insincere and the notion that the sinner’s refusal is anything but his own wickedness.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is God’s sovereignty in hardening. Moses sent sincere words of peace to Sihon, who refused of his own obstinacy; yet the LORD hardened his spirit for judgment, delivering him into Israel’s hand. God hath mercy on whom He will, and whom He will He hardeneth — leaving the sinner without excuse, yet accomplishing His eternal counsel.
